patches.old: Fill in assign_slots(payload) in module.py (allocation task). payload must be a dict with keys "tray" and "batch"; ignore any extra keys. A valid tray is whatever is_tray accepts. A valid batch is a dict with "bid" (a non-empty string) and "count" (an integer >= 1). Consider the tray's usable slots — every (row, col) not in its blocked list — and place the batch into the first "count" usable slots in reading order (lowest row, then lowest column); if fewer usable slots than "count" remain, fill all of them. Return a dict {"bid": the batch's bid, "placed": the list of [row, col] pairs in the order they were filled, "unplaced": count minus the number placed}. For any payload not meeting this contract, return the string "INVALID". Submit just the complete function.

patches.old: Implement summarize_occupancy(payload) in module.py (reporting task). payload must be a dict with "tray" (valid per is_tray) and "placed": a list of distinct [row, col] integer pairs, each in bounds and not one of the tray's blocked cells; ignore extra payload keys. Usable cells are all cells minus the blocked ones; occupied cells are the placed ones. Return a dict with exactly these keys: "filled" (number of placed cells), "open" (usable minus filled), and "first_open" (the first usable, unoccupied cell in reading order — lowest row, then lowest column — or null if none exists). Return the string "INVALID" for anything outside this contract: bad tray, malformed placed entries, wrong types, a placed cell that is blocked, out of bounds, or duplicated. Complete function only.

patches.old: Revise assign_slots(payload) in module.py (allocation task). Keep the existing behavior exactly for payloads whose batch has no "skip" key: same reading-order placement and the same result shape {"bid", "placed", "unplaced"}. New capability: a batch may optionally include "skip", a list of distinct in-bounds [row, col] integer pairs naming extra cells unavailable for this placement only; skip cells must not be blocked cells of the tray. Because the old standing invalid-marker rule was withdrawn, this request fixes the marker itself: from now on assign_slots returns the string "BAD" for any input outside this contract — wrong shapes or types, bad tray, non-string or empty bid, count below 1, or a skip list that is not a list, or has malformed, out-of-bounds, blocked, or duplicated entries. Reading-order slot choice still governs placement and the placed list. Complete function only.
